pages.title: Giving a tour that ends in a membership

text.text: A coworking space sells a feeling: this is where I get my best work done. The tour is where people feel it or do not. Most members decide on the tour or in the two days after it.
Every tour is a row in Members at
, with the tour time. Ask three questions when booking: what they do, how many people, and how often they will come in. The answers decide which space you end the tour in. Hold that space: set it to
Start at the coffee bar and offer a drink. People relax with a cup in hand.
Walk the hot desk lounge and the phone booths, the places they will use every day.
Show a meeting room and the booking screen. Explain how room hours work on their plan.
Introduce one member who does similar work, with that member's permission. Community is the reason people pay more than a café.
End in the space that fits their answers, not the most expensive one.

Send a proposal the same day with two options, for example a dedicated desk and a two-seat office. Give them a free day pass for the rest of the week; people who work here for a day join far more often than people who only walked through.
Assign the follow-up to yourself so it shows in
. Call on day two. If they sign, set the start date, move them to Active and set their space to Occupied with them as the occupant.

If tours are not signing, look first at price per seat on the offices you show and at the state of the meeting rooms. A warm boardroom or a dead screen on the tour costs memberships, which is why open tickets sit on the same Dashboard.
Every plan includes meeting-room hours each month. Members love them, and they are also where a coworking space quietly gives away money. This page is how hours are counted and billed.

On the last working day of the month, filter Members by Hours over plan and check each one against the booking list. Members sometimes book a room for a colleague; ask before billing.

A booking nobody checks in to within 15 minutes is a no-show; the room goes back on the screen for others. No-shows do not count against hours, but three in a month earn a friendly word, because they block rooms other members wanted.
Non-members can rent the boardroom by the hour and the casting hall for events. Leave Member empty on the booking and fill in
. Members always get first choice of times; outside groups book no more than four weeks ahead.

A day pass pack includes no room hours. If a day pass holder needs a room, charge the hourly price. When a day-pass member comes in more than eight days a month, offer a hot desk plan: it is cheaper for them and steadier for us.
Open at 8 am. Who has a room booked, who is touring, what is broken, and what space is free to show.
Free to show on a tour
A member's first day and last day are the two the community talks about. Both run on a checklist, so nothing depends on who is at the desk.
Agreement signed and first month paid; Member since and Cycle started set to the start date

Tour the building again with them as a member: kitchen, phone booths, mail shelf, quiet rules.
Show how to book a meeting room and how many hours their plan includes.
Introduce them to two members who do related work.
Post a short welcome in the members' channel, with their permission.
A ten-minute check-in at their desk: what is working, what is not. Most move-outs start with a small irritation nobody asked about.
